terms.gloss: a roof sloping two ways, like a comb
evidence: Fest. p. 212–213 Müll.: pectenātum tēctum dīcitur ā similitūdine pectinis in duās partēs dēvexum, ut testūdinātum in quattuor (Lewis & Short s.v. pectinō)
terms.comment: Festus’s name for the roof that slopes two ways from the ridge, as a hipped roof, testūdinātum, slopes four ways. Festus writes pectenātum; Lewis & Short’s headword is pectinātus.

phrases.english: a roof sloping to either side

sources: Lewis & Short: tectum · Lewis & Short: declivis
